unchanged. To change text code, edit the template and re-run `bootstrap.sh --steps fill_text,dte,...`.

## Text policy

**Running dialogue and message text from the original is never quoted in a tracked file** (docs,
comments, notes, task text, harness data, test fixtures). **Identifiers may be named**: room titles, item
names and UI labels such as FANTASY WORLD, for identification. Refer to a message by its source line
(`[X-ALL.TXT line 733]`, or the key `X-ALL:733`), never by its words. Which strings are which is decided by
source region in `tools/textsplit/categories.txt` (room table, item table, UI boxes versus
the `PEOPLE TALKING` / `DOING THINGS` / `ALL DEAD` message sections; unknown lines count as messages).
Harness scripts that need the real strings for a pixel or text comparison read them from the generated,
gitignored `harness/orig_text.lua`, never from literals.

Classification finding: `game_text.json` carries no category, only `file`, `line`, `raw`, `decoded`. The
category is derived from the source **region** (`categories.txt`: tag + line range, first match wins,
fail closed). X-ALL.TXT lines 401-503 are room titles, 1081+ item names, the title/credits and the
coin/inventory UI boxes are UI labels, and lines 540-1050 (the three message sections) are messages.

Gates (both run in `scripts/export-public.sh` on the staged tree):

- `textsplit check-public --docs --list FILES` needs your `game_text.json` (`$GPF_GAME_TEXT` or the default
  path) and is **fail-closed when it is present**. It fails on a message string that reads as a quote (an
  upper-case match of >= 3 words or >= 12 characters, or 4+ words in any case) and on a run of >= 3 message
  strings starting within a 6-line window (dialogue split into short rows). Identifiers pass in any number.
  `tools/textsplit/allow.txt` lets ordinary prose through (lower-case only for several words).
- `tools/textsplit/check_docs_nodata.sh` needs **no user data** and always runs: it fails on a run of >= 3
  colon-encoded upper-case segments (the source's own form: colons in place of spaces) unless listed in `nodata_allow.txt`
  (identifiers only). Limitation: it cannot see dialogue written in plain words; that is caught only by the
  user-data gate. When there is no `game_text.json` the export prints `doc-text gate skipped: no user data`.

To fix a finding, run `textsplit scrub --orig-json extracted/game_text.json --list FILES` (dry run; `--apply`
writes) and review `git diff --stat`; it replaces message strings by `[X-ALL.TXT line N]`.

Export gates (`scripts/export-public.sh`): `tools/textsplit/check_templates.sh` (no user data
needed: templates may contain only `@orig` keys and `port_only.txt` strings) and `textsplit
check-public` when the user's `game_text.json` is present.

## Not needed to build (dropped, regenerable only for analysis)

Preview PNGs (`extracted/*_frames`, `art_preview`), the ZX
ground-truth probe dumps under `harness/probes/`, WIP patches, and `baselines/*` logs.
Harness runs that need the original use your own tape and Spectrum ROM under MAME.

## Known gaps (tracked as tasks)

- ~~No script ran the extractors / split the frames~~ -- closed: `tools/bootstrap.sh` (steps `extract`, `split`); `tools/clean_generated.sh` lists/removes the generated set; `docs/BUILD-HASHES.txt` pins the five artifacts.
- `extracted/art_preview`, `room36_cart.rom`, `harness/probes/t0209_solidity.json` have no
  documented producer (none is needed to build).
- ~~Absolute personal paths in extracted JSON~~ -- closed: the extractors now relativize `source_file` and the bootstrap passes relative paths.
- ~~Text built from committed `target/text_src*`; `fill_text` a no-op~~ -- closed: `text_src*` are generated by `textsplit fill`; hand-authored `room36.asm`, `title_mix3.asm`, `win_mix3.asm` and the templates are tracked and exported (the export scan allowlists them in `.public-scan-allow`).

; T0148: update_dragon + dragon_flames, CODE ONLY, split out of gameplay.asm
; and staged to CODE_DEST ($8000+, immediately below BANNER_BUF) -- the
; proof-of-concept that RESIDENT CODE, not just room data, can be staged
; and unpacked at boot exactly the way room data already is (NOTES.md
; "Why a 64K machine is tighter" -- the relief valve nobody had tried).
;
; WHY THIS ROUTINE: it is room 54's dragon update, called from exactly one
; site (room36.asm mainloop's `jsr update_dragon`, gameplay-only, long
; after new_game/show_title have run) and self-contained -- every local it
; touches (dgf_i, dgf_x, udr_n, udr_slot, udr_head_y, dragon_swing,
; dragon_delay, dragon_asleep, dragon_fire, dragon_headfrm, dragon_flame_n,
; dragon_flame_x) is a plain fcb/fdb, left resident in gameplay.asm at its
; ORIGINAL low address -- only the CODE moves, per T0148's brief. draw_dragon
; (room36.asm) and dragon_necky (room36.asm) read those same variables and
; are UNCHANGED: absolute addressing does not care where the code reading
; them lives, only where the variables themselves are, and those did not
; move.
;
; DELIVERY: packed as its own LZSS stream riding the title's load-time
; holes, the same mechanism as block C (rooms 39/23, T0125) but as a
; SEPARATE stream (mktitle's new --extra2), not appended to block C's --
; concatenating would force it to decode contiguously with block C's
; destination, colliding with the "top of the room-growth span, below
; BANNER_BUF" placement this task calls for. See room36.asm's CODE_DEST
; and tools/roompack/src/bin/mktitle.rs.
;
; Unpacked once at boot, by logic_low.asm's unpack_d, called from
; boot_code.asm's show_title right after unpack_c and before the title
; transpose -- i.e. strictly before new_game, strictly before mainloop can
; ever call update_dragon.
;
; WALL HIT, then a REAL fix (not a workaround): lwasm 4.24 (`lwasm
; --version`) computes relative-branch offsets INSIDE a `phase` block using
; the PHYSICAL (org) address of one operand and the LOGICAL (phase)
; address of the other -- confirmed with a 2-instruction repro (`beq` two
; bytes from its target, `org $1000 / phase $9000`: the assembled offset
; came out as (true_offset - (phase-org)), i.e. off by exactly the
; org/phase gap, not by a rounding slip). Short branches usually then trip
; lwasm's own overflow check and fail loud; LONG branches (lbeq etc) have
; enough range to silently accept the WRONG offset and assemble clean --
; tried first, looked like a fix because the build succeeded, but the
; emulator proved it wasn't: `update_dragon` branched into unmapped memory
; every time cur_room=54, and breathsfx.lua's harness (harness/breathsfx.lua)
; caught it stone cold -- dragon_swing/dragon_fire/rng_ctr never moved for
; 300 frames where the unstaged original took under 500. rate.lua and the
; other harnesses in T0148's verify list did NOT catch it (a wrong branch
; into RAM that happens to be zero-filled just executes NEG opcodes
; harmlessly until an RTS turns up by chance -- no crash, no hang, just the
; routine quietly doing nothing). Moral: a routine with no branches at all
; (every room-data block before this one) can't expose this bug; a harness
; that pokes the routine's OWN state, not just "did the game keep running",
; is what caught it.
;
; THE FIX: this file is not assembled inside `phase` at all any more --
; room36.asm orgs straight to CODE_DEST (see its own comment). Pass 1 is
; the raw/STAGE_GEN measurement pass and is never loaded on real hardware
; (same as block C above it), so assembling directly at the real $8000+
; address costs nothing and every branch offset is then correct by
; construction, exactly as the org==phase control case of the same repro
; confirmed. Branches here are back to their natural short forms.
update_dragon
        lda cur_room
        cmpa #54
        beq udr_inroom
        rts
udr_inroom
        ; already fully retracted and asleep: the source's own `ret z`
        ; -- nothing more ever changes, so touch nothing.
        lda dragon_asleep
        beq udr_awake
        lda dragon_swing
        cmpa #-8
        bne udr_awake
        rts
udr_awake
        ldx #actor_ram
        lda #ACTOR_COUNT
        sta udr_n
udr_find
        lda ,x
        cmpa cur_room
        bne udr_findnext
        lda 1,x
        cmpa #ROU_DRAGON
        beq udr_found
udr_findnext
        leax ACTOR_STRIDE,x
        dec udr_n
        bne udr_find
        rts
udr_found
        ; T0255: X-ALL dragonrou -> trytostartbreathing runs BEFORE the swing and the head are drawn, and when it
        ; starts a breath it `pop hl / jp alreadybreathing`: that very tick keeps the swing, draws the head with the
        ; breath frame (110) and runs the first flame step.  The roll used to follow the head, one tick late.
        tst dragon_asleep
        bne udr_headgo            ; a sleeping dragon never breathes fire
        tst dragon_fire
        bne udr_headgo
        ; not currently breathing: the source's own random 5/256 per-
        ; tick chance (`justrandomfire` -- this build has no golden-egg
        ; state to special-case, so that's the only path that applies).
        ; Reuses the free-running LFSR (rng_step, room36.asm) rather
        ; than a second generator -- it is already sampled by unrelated
        ; subsystems every pass, which is exactly what makes it a valid
        ; source of "unpredictable" bits for this one too.
        lda rng_ctr
        cmpa #5
        bhs udr_headgo
        lda #1
        sta dragon_fire
        jsr play_breath          ; T0111: sndfx 10, X-ALL.TXT startbreath
udr_headgo
        jsr dragon_head

        ; asleep and only just now reached -8: this is the LAST active
        ; tick (matches the source drawing once more before the next
        ; call's `ret z`) -- fall through and draw/collide-check the
        ; flame state normally; draw_dragon will stop after this pass.

        tst dragon_asleep
        bne udr_nofire
        tst dragon_fire
        beq udr_nofire
        jsr dragon_flames         ; positions + collision + the wrap/inc
udr_nofire
        rts

; dragon_head: X = the dragon's actor slot (actor_ram for room 54, actor_init_tape for room 40).
; Advances the swing (asleep: retract toward -8; awake: the triangle wave, frozen mid-breath),
; picks the head frame, writes the head's CURRENT state into the slot and kills Dizzy on a head
; hit. Shared by update_dragon and tape_code.asm's update_dragon40 (T0254: they were two copies).
; Clobbers A, B, X, Y; sets udr_slot and udr_head_y.
dragon_head
        stx udr_slot

        ; T0133: proxsleep used to fire here on mere proximity (any
        ; visit to the box). The source only fires it via `justexitinvent`
        ; -> checkproximity when the [X-ALL.TXT line 642] is dropped in the
        ; box -- see check_drop_trigger's cdt_potion branch, which is now
        ; the only place dragon_asleep gets latched (plus the debug key,
        ; DBG_DRAGON_KEY below).

        lda dragon_asleep
        beq udr_swingawake
        ; asleep, still retracting: decrement toward -8, no swing-wave,
        ; no fire (a sleeping dragon does not breathe).
        lda dragon_swing
        deca
        cmpa #-8
        bge udr_haveswing         ; SIGNED compare -- floor at -8. (An
                                    ; unsigned bhs/blo here would be wrong:
                                    ; swing spans both small positive
                                    ; values (0..16) and small negative
                                    ; ones (-8..-1), which as unsigned
                                    ; bytes are 0..16 vs 248..255 -- the
                                    ; two ranges sort backwards from
                                    ; their signed order.)
        lda #-8
        bra udr_haveswing
udr_swingawake
        ; breathing freezes the swing exactly where it was (the
        ; source's own `alreadybreathing` skip) -- only advance the
        ; triangle wave when NOT currently mid-breath.
        lda dragon_fire
        bne udr_haveswing_cur
        lda dragon_delay
        inca
        anda #31
        sta dragon_delay
        cmpa #16
        blo udr_swinglo
        nega
        adda #32
        bra udr_haveswing
udr_swinglo
udr_haveswing
        sta dragon_swing
        bra udr_swingdone
udr_haveswing_cur
        lda dragon_swing
udr_swingdone

        ; head position + frame, from the (possibly just-updated) swing
        lda #DRAGON_ORIGY
        suba dragon_swing
        sta udr_head_y
        lda #109                  ; idle / second half of a breath
        ldb dragon_fire
        beq udr_headframeok       ; not breathing at all: 109
        decb
        cmpb #16
        bhs udr_headframeok       ; second half of the cycle: still 109
        lda #110                  ; first half: mid-roar
udr_headframeok
        sta dragon_headfrm

        ; write the head's CURRENT animated state into the slot so
        ; actor_hit (which reads frame/x/y straight from it) tests
        ; against where the head actually is this tick, not its rest
        ; position.
        ldx udr_slot
        lda dragon_headfrm
        sta 4,x
        lda #DRAGON_HEAD_X
        sta 2,x
        lda udr_head_y
        sta 3,x
        ldy udr_slot
        jsr actor_hit
        tsta
        beq udr_nothead
        ldx #msg_dragon
        jsr kill_dizzy_msg
udr_nothead
        rts

; dragon_flames: dragon_fire is nonzero. Computes this tick's visible
; flame positions (X-ALL.TXT's `printdragonflame`, simulated in Python
; before writing this to confirm the six-iteration form is exact),
; tests each against Dizzy, and advances the cycle.
dragon_flames
        clr dragon_flame_n
        lda #6
        sta dgf_i
dgf_loop
        lda dgf_i
        asla                     ; A = dgf_i*2
        adda #68                 ; A = dgf_i*2 + 68
        suba dragon_fire         ; A = pos = dgf_i*2 - dragon_fire + 68
        cmpa #50
        blo dgf_next               ; pos < 50: not yet visible
        cmpa #68
        bhs dgf_next               ; pos >= 68: already past the mouth

        ; visible: pixel_x = (pos-32)*4, record it and test the hit
        suba #32
        lsla
        lsla
        sta dgf_x
        sta ah_bx
        lda udr_head_y
        adda #8
        sta ah_by
        lda aspr_112_w
        sta ah_bw
        lda aspr_112_h
        jsr aabb_test          ; T0221 (was 7 bytes inline)
        beq dgf_nothit
        ldx #msg_dragonfire
        jsr kill_dizzy_msg
dgf_nothit
        ldb dragon_flame_n
        ldx #dragon_flame_x
        abx
        lda dgf_x
        sta ,x
        inc dragon_flame_n
dgf_next
        dec dgf_i
        bne dgf_loop

        lda dragon_fire
        inca
        cmpa #48
        blo dgf_storefire
        clra
dgf_storefire
        sta dragon_fire
        rts

; T0148: the local variables, moved here WITH the code (see gameplay.asm's
; own note at the old site for why they could not stay resident below
; $8000 -- pass 1/pass 2 disagree on low-memory addresses by exactly the
; size gap between STAGE_LZ's two boot mechanisms, and these are the first
; staged bytes that ever referenced a low address). draw_dragon and
; dragon_necky (room36.asm, unmoved) still reach dragon_swing/dragon_
; asleep/dragon_headfrm/dragon_fire/dragon_flame_n/dragon_flame_x/
; udr_head_y by plain absolute addressing -- staged_syms.asm exports their
; CODE_DEST-relative addresses explicitly for pass 2 (tools/stage_pack.sh),
; the same way it exports update_dragon itself.
dgf_i        fcb 0
dgf_x        fcb 0

udr_n       fcb 0
udr_slot    fdb 0
udr_head_y  fcb 0

dragon_swing    fcb 0    ; signed: 0..16 awake, decrementing to -8 asleep
dragon_delay    fcb 0    ; 0..31, drives the triangle wave
dragon_asleep   fcb 0    ; latched permanently by the proxsleep trigger
dragon_fire     fcb 0    ; 0 = not breathing; 1..47 = a breath cycle
dragon_headfrm  fcb 109  ; 109 or 110, precomputed for draw_dragon
; T0148: dragon_flame_x (rmb, no emitted bytes) moved BEFORE dragon_flame_n
; rather than after it -- lwasm does not emit trailing bytes for an `rmb`
; that ends a block with nothing after it, so the DECB block stage_pack.sh
; extracts came out 6 bytes short of code_staged_end-code_staged_start
; (caught by whole_block's own length check, not guessed). Ending on a
; real `fcb` keeps the block's actual emitted length matching the map.
dragon_flame_x  fcb 0,0,0,0,0,0   ; T0148: explicit zeros, not rmb -- lwasm emits
                 ; nothing for an rmb, and stage_pack's length guard
                 ; compares emitted bytes against the map    ; their pixel x, precomputed by dragon_flames
dragon_flame_n  fcb 0    ; how many of dragon_flame_x are valid this tick

# 🏴‍☠️ Treasure Island Dizzy - Enhanced Canvas Game

A modern remake of the classic **Treasure Island Dizzy** game, built with vanilla JavaScript and HTML5 Canvas. This enhanced version features improved graphics, sound effects, background music, and smooth animations.

![Game Preview](https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-Playable-brightgreen)
![Tech Stack](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tech-JavaScript%20%7C%20Canvas%20%7C%20Web%20Audio-blue)

## 🎮 Features

### 🎨 Enhanced Graphics
- **Animated Player Character**: Blinking eyes, directional facing, animated arms/legs during movement
- **Dynamic Environment**: Parallax clouds, swaying palm trees, animated ocean waves
- **Visual Effects**: Particle systems for jumping and treasure collection, floating animations
- **Multiple Treasure Types**: Coins, gems, and crowns with different point values
- **Smooth Animations**: 60fps gameplay with smooth movement and transitions

### 🔊 Audio System
- **Procedural Sound Effects**: Jump sounds, collection chimes, footstep noises
- **Background Music**: Simple procedural melody loop using Web Audio API
- **Interactive Audio**: Click or press any key to start audio (browser requirement)
- **Cross-Browser Compatible**: Fallback handling for audio support

### 🎯 Gameplay Features
- **Platform Mechanics**: Jump on elevated platforms to reach special treasures
- **Win Condition**: Collect all treasures to complete the level
- **Score System**: Different treasures give different point values
- **Physics**: Realistic gravity, friction, and collision detection

## 🚀 How to Play

1. **Movement**: Use arrow keys (←→) to move left and right
2. **Jump**: Press up arrow (↑) to jump
3. **Audio**: Click anywhere or press any key to start background music
4. **Objective**: Collect all treasures scattered around the island
5. **Scoring**: 
   - 🪙 Gold Coins: 100 points
   - 💎 Gems: 200 points  
   - 👑 Crowns: 300 points

## 🛠️ Technical Implementation

### Architecture
- **Object-Oriented Design**: Main `Game` class handling all game logic
- **Component System**: Separate systems for player, treasures, particles, audio
- **Performance Optimized**: Efficient rendering and animation loops

### Technologies Used
- **HTML5 Canvas**: 2D graphics rendering
- **Web Audio API**: Procedural sound generation and background music
- **Vanilla JavaScript**: No external dependencies
- **CSS3**: Responsive styling and layout

### File Structure
```
├── index.html          # Main HTML file
├── styles.css          # Game styling
├── audio.js           # Audio system (standalone)
├── game.js            # Main game implementation
└── README.md          # This file
```

## 🎵 Audio Features

The game features a complete audio system built with the Web Audio API:

- **Procedural Music**: Simple C major scale melody that loops continuously
- **Dynamic Sound Effects**: 
  - Jump: 400Hz sine wave burst
  - Collection: 800Hz square wave chime
  - Footsteps: 200Hz sawtooth noise
- **Volume Control**: Balanced audio levels for optimal experience
- **Browser Compatibility**: Graceful fallbacks for unsupported browsers

## 🎨 Visual Features

### Player Character
- Egg-shaped protagonist inspired by the original Dizzy character
- Animated eyes with blinking cycle
- Directional facing based on movement
- Smooth arm and leg animations during walking/jumping
- Bounce effect on landing

### Environment
- Gradient sky background
- Parallax-scrolling clouds
- Animated ocean waves
- Swaying palm trees with physics-based movement
- Detailed treasure chest and platform elements
- Dynamic particle effects

### Special Effects
- Jump dust particles when launching
- Sparkle effects when collecting treasures
- Floating animation on collectible items
- Shadow rendering under player character
- Glow effects on treasures

## 🌊 Game Mechanics

### Physics System
- Realistic gravity and momentum
- Friction for smooth movement feel
- Platform collision detection
- Boundary constraint handling

### Treasure System
- Three distinct treasure types with visual differences
- Collision detection with visual feedback
- Score accumulation with immediate UI updates
- Win condition tracking

### Particle System
- Dust particles for environmental interaction
- Sparkle effects for treasure collection
- Life-cycle management with alpha fading
- Physics-based movement with gravity

## 🔧 Setup and Installation

1. **Clone the repository:**
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/jane-alesi/game-demo.git
   cd game-demo
   ```

2. **Open in browser:**
   ```bash
   # Simply open index.html in any modern web browser
   open index.html  # macOS
   start index.html # Windows
   ```

3. **Or serve locally:**
   ```bash
   # Using Python
   python -m http.server 8000
   
   # Using Node.js
   npx http-server
   
   # Then open http://localhost:8000
   ```

## 🎯 Game Controls

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| ← | Move Left |
| → | Move Right |
| ↑ | Jump |
| Click/Any Key | Start Audio |

## 📱 Browser Compatibility

- ✅ **Chrome/Chromium**: Full support
- ✅ **Firefox**: Full support  
- ✅ **Safari**: Full support
- ✅ **Edge**: Full support
- ⚠️ **Mobile**: Touch controls not implemented

## 🎨 Development Notes

This game was created as a demonstration of:
- Modern vanilla JavaScript game development
- HTML5 Canvas 2D graphics programming
- Web Audio API implementation
- Object-oriented game architecture
- Performance optimization techniques

### Inspired by:
- **Original Treasure Island Dizzy** (1988) by the Oliver Twins
- Classic British platformer design principles
- Modern web game development practices

## 🏆 Future Enhancements

Potential improvements for future versions:
- Touch controls for mobile devices
- Multiple levels and enemy characters
- Inventory system for puzzle mechanics
- Save/load game state
- High score tracking
- More complex physics interactions

## 📄 License

This project is open source and available under the MIT License. The original Dizzy IP belongs to its respective owners - this is a tribute/educational implementation.

---

*Demonstrating modern web game development techniques*

# kwik_snax

Some food hacks I can't get enough of.

## Crappuccino

Ingredients:
- Instant coffee.
- Oatly Barista, or cow's milk.

Method:
- Boil a small amount of water in a kettle.
- Put two teaspoons of instant coffee in a cup.
- Pour just enough water over the instant coffee to dissolve it while stirring.
- Shake up the milk to make it frothy.
- Pour over the coffee to complete the cup.
- Microwave for ~30 seconds to warm it up.

☕

## Tiramisu

Ingredients:
- 1 can of Carnation condensed milk.
- 2x 250g tubs of mascarpone.
- Trifle sponge fingers, or a box of trifle sponges.
- Cocoa powder to sprinkle.
- Alcohol: 50ml of Amaretto or Rum.
- 50ml of strong black coffee.

Method:
- Place the sponges in a dish.
- Tip the coffee and alcohol over the sponges. Don’t make them soggy.
- Dust with cocoa powder.
- Beat together the mascarpone and condensed milk until smooth and not runny. Pour over the sponges, covering completely.
- Give a good coating of cocoa powder on top. Can add some chocolate shavings if you have them.
